title: Environment Variables
subtitle: $PATH, export, .bashrc, .profile — making the shell work for you
author: KERNAL Team

content.code:
# Read a variable
echo $HOME          # /home/alice
echo $USER          # alice
echo $SHELL         # /bin/bash
echo $PATH          # /usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:...

# Set a variable (only current shell session)
NAME="Alice"
echo $NAME          # Alice

# export: make a variable available to child processes
export DATABASE_URL="postgresql://localhost/myapp"
export NODE_ENV="development"

# View all environment variables
env
printenv
printenv PATH       # print just one variable

# Unset a variable
unset DATABASE_URL

# Set for a single command
NODE_ENV=production node app.js    # only sets for that command

# PATH is a colon-separated list of directories
echo $PATH
# /usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin:/home/alice/.local/bin

# When you type 'node', the shell searches each PATH dir in order
# and runs the first 'node' it finds
which node    # /usr/local/bin/node

# Add a directory to PATH
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"   # prepend (higher priority)
export PATH="$PATH:/opt/myapp/bin"     # append (lower priority)

# Common additions to PATH:
# ~/.local/bin  — user-installed tools
# ~/.cargo/bin  — Rust (cargo install)
# ~/go/bin      — Go binaries
# /opt/homebrew/bin — macOS Homebrew (Apple Silicon)

# .bashrc — loaded for every interactive non-login bash shell
# Put: aliases, functions, PATH additions, prompt customization

# .bash_profile / .profile — loaded for login shells
# Put: environment variables, PATH (loaded once at login)

# .zshrc — same as .bashrc but for zsh

# Edit your .bashrc:
nano ~/.bashrc
# Add:
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
export EDITOR="vim"
alias ll='ls -la'
alias gs='git status'
alias gp='git push'

# Reload without opening a new terminal
source ~/.bashrc   # or: . ~/.bashrc

content.text: Put export statements (env vars, PATH) in ~/.profile or ~/.bash_profile so they load once at login. Put aliases and functions in ~/.bashrc for interactive sessions. Both files are loaded in most setups — when in doubt, use ~/.bashrc.

questions.question: You add export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH" to your .bashrc and run source ~/.bashrc. You then open a new terminal. Is the PATH change permanent?
options: No — source only affects the current session temporarily
Yes — .bashrc is loaded on every new interactive bash session
No — you need to put it in /etc/environment for it to persist
No — environment variables are always reset on new sessions
questions.explanation: .bashrc is executed every time you open a new interactive non-login shell (every new terminal window/tab). So changes to ~/.bashrc persist permanently — every new terminal will load it. source ~/.bashrc applies the change to the current session without needing to open a new one.

faq.q: Where should I store sensitive environment variables (API keys)?
faq.a: Not in .bashrc — that file gets committed to git by accident. Use a .env file in your project (and add .env to .gitignore), then load it with a tool like direnv (automatic per-directory env) or explicitly with export $(cat .env | xargs) in your session. For production, use your hosting platform's secret management (Heroku config vars, Railway variables, Kubernetes secrets).

examples: DATABASE_URL, SECRET_KEY, API_KEY — the standard way to configure 12-factor apps without hardcoding secrets in source code
$PATH manipulation is done by every version manager: nvm, rbenv, pyenv — they prepend their bin directory to $PATH to shadow system versions
